title: The wrong bishop
tagline: Bishop, rook pawn, wrong corner: draw

principles.prompt: White has an h-pawn and a light-squared bishop. Why is Black's draw already in sight?
principles.answer: h8 is a dark square, so the bishop can never control the queening corner. If Black's king reaches it, stalemate defends everything: wrong bishop, rook pawn, draw.

principles.prompt: How do you tell instantly whether a bishop is the 'wrong' one?
principles.answer: Look at the promotion corner's colour. Bishop doesn't match it = wrong. Only rook pawns have this problem — every other pawn queens on a square the defender can't fortress.

principles.prompt: You're defending against rook pawn + wrong bishop. What's the whole plan?
principles.answer: King to the corner by the shortest road, then stay. Material, checks, the pawn's speed — none of it matters if you arrive. And a one-colour diagonal road can never be blocked by the other-coloured bishop.

principles.prompt: You're the one attacking with rook pawn + wrong bishop. What's your only winning idea?
principles.answer: Fence the defending king out of the corner before it gets there. Once it's in, there is no eviction — offer the draw.

demos.title: The fortress that cannot fall
demos.intro: Black is a bishop and pawn down, king in the corner. Watch White try everything and achieve nothing.

steps.note: Black's entire plan: shuffle between g8 and h8.
The pawn marches. It doesn't matter.
Closer. The bishop, meanwhile, watches light squares — h8 is dark.
— and now it can never queen: the king sits on h8 and no piece White owns can touch a dark square.
Stalemate. g8 is covered by the pawn, g7 by the king, h7 is occupied. Half a point each — the wrong bishop in one picture.

demos.title: Slam the door
demos.intro: Same material, one difference: Black's king isn't in the corner yet. White's only winning idea — keep it out.

steps.note: The door: from f7 White's king owns g8, and Black can never reach the corner.
Black tries to walk over anyway.
With the fortress fenced off, the pawn simply runs.
Black changes plan: chase the pawn.
Count it — the box from Tier 1. The king is outside.
Note what Black couldn't play: f5. The bishop's c2-f5 diagonal had the road fenced all along — that's its one real job here.
Queened. The fortress never formed because the king never got in — that's the whole attacking plan.

tests.title: The diagonal road
tests.intro: Bishop and pawn down, king across the board. The h-pawn queens in five — and the corner is exactly five away.

wrong.Kc2: Count it: the pawn needs five moves, and from c2 the corner is five more — one too many. Only the diagonal keeps pace.
wrong.Kb3: Sideways wastes the tempo you don't have. The diagonal b2-c3-d4-e5-f6-g7 arrives exactly in time.
wrong.Kb1: Away from the corner — the pawn queens unchallenged. Head for g7, along the diagonal.

hints: The pawn queens in five moves. Draw your road to g7 — you have exactly five, and only one road fits.
Kc3 — the diagonal b2-c3-d4-e5-f6-g7. Note the bishop can never block it: every square on it is dark.

tests.explanationAfter: You walked the dark diagonal the light bishop can never touch, arriving at g7 the move before the pawn queens. Now h8=Q is met by Kxh8 — and if White waits instead, you step into the corner and the fortress from this lesson holds forever.

tests.title: Through b7
tests.intro: An a-pawn and a dark-squared bishop — the wrong one for a8. The corner road has exactly one gate.

wrong.Kc8: b8 belongs to the bishop — via c8 you arrive a tempo late, and Kb6 seals the door for good. Go through b7.
wrong.Kd7: The corner road runs through b7, and only b7. Anything else lets Kb6 wall you out.
wrong.Kd8: Too slow — Kb6 comes, the pawn gets its escort, and the corner is a memory.

hints: The bishop owns b8, his king covers b6. Which square still leads to a8?
Kb7 — the one gate. From there the corner is yours whatever White plays.

tests.explanationAfter: b7 was the only door the bishop and king left open. From there a8 can't be denied — and a king in the corner against the wrong bishop is a fortress no material can crack. Even grabbing the pawn works: king and bishop alone can't mate.

tests.title: Only the check
tests.intro: This bishop is the right colour — the corner is a trap, not a fortress. But Black has no moves at all, so choose with care.

wrong.Bd6: Stalemate! Black's king has no legal move — any quiet move throws away the win. Only a check works here.
wrong.Be7: Stalemate! Black's king has no legal move — any quiet move throws away the win. Only a check works here.
wrong.Kf7: Kxh7! Your king was the pawn's only guard — with it gone, king and bishop can't mate: draw.
wrong.Kf6: Kxh7! Your king was the pawn's only guard — with it gone, king and bishop can't mate: draw.

hints: Black's only squares are g8 (your pawn covers it) and g7 (your king does). What does that mean for every non-checking move?
Bc3 — the long dark diagonal: check, g7 covered twice, g8 covered by the pawn. Mate.

tests.explanationAfter: The right-coloured bishop turns the corner from fortress into coffin — but only by force. With Black's king out of moves, every quiet move was stalemate; the diagonal check was mate. Right bishop: win. Wrong bishop: none of this works.

tests.title: Downhill diagonal
tests.intro: Black's a-pawn queens on a1, a dark square — and his bishop watches light ones. You know where your king is going.

wrong.Kf8: Off the road — the pawn runs in five and from f8 the corner is six away. g7-f6-e5-d4-c3-b2 is the only walk that fits.
wrong.Kg8: Away from the corner — the pawn queens with time to spare. Head down the g7-b2 diagonal.
wrong.Kh6: Grabbing the bishop costs the race — the pawn queens while you're snacking. The corner, nothing else.

hints: His pawn needs five moves; the a1-corner zone is exactly five away. One road fits — and his bishop can't touch a single square of it.
Kf6 — the dark diagonal g7-f6-e5-d4-c3-b2, arriving just in time.

tests.explanationAfter: The same race as the h-pawn drill, downhill: five pushes against five dark steps the light bishop can never block. On b2 you meet a1=Q+ with Kxa1 — and if the pawn hesitates, you claim the corner and the wrong-bishop fortress claims the game.
